items.prompt: White to move. Capture a black piece with the rook.

claims.statement: The rook cannot reach a6: its own pawn on a3 is in the way and a rook does not jump.
The rook on a1 can reach exactly a2, b1, c1 and d1.
Rxd1 wins the knight.
Rxd1 is among the engine's best moves.

hints: Look at the rook's file and its rank. Which black pieces share them?
One black piece sits on the rook's file, but something stands between.
The other black piece is on the first rank with nothing in between.
items.explain: The bishop on a6 shares the rook's file, but the pawn on a3 stands in between and a rook cannot jump it. The knight on d1 is on the rook's rank with free squares between, so Rxd1 is the capture available.

feedback_by_move.a1a6: A rook cannot jump over its own pawn on a3, so Rxa6 is not a legal move here.
feedback_by_move.a1a2: Ra2 is legal, but it stops against the pawn on a3 and captures nothing.

items.prompt: White to move. Capture a black piece with the rook.

claims.statement: The rook cannot land on a3: it holds White's own bishop.
The rook on a1 can reach exactly a2, b1, c1, d1 and e1.
Rxe1 wins the knight.
Rxe1 is among the engine's best moves.

hints: List every square the rook can reach before choosing.
A square holding one of your own pieces is never on that list.
The target is on the first rank, to the right of the rook.
items.explain: A rook may take an enemy piece but may not land on its own piece, so a3 is not an option. The first rank is open up to the knight on e1, and Rxe1 captures it.

feedback_by_move.a1a3: Ra3 is not a legal move: the square holds White's own bishop, and a rook cannot land on its own piece.
feedback_by_move.a1b1: Rb1 is legal, but it only moves along the rank and captures nothing yet.

items.prompt: White to move. Is there a rook move that wins material? Play it.

claims.statement: The rook may capture the knight on d5.
The rook cannot pass through the knight to d8.
The knight on d5 is attacked and undefended.
Rxd5+ wins the knight.

hints: Which black pieces stand on the rook's file?
A rook may take the first enemy piece on its line.
Check whether that piece has a defender.
items.explain: The knight on d5 is the first enemy piece on the d-file and nothing defends it, so the rook can simply take it. Squares behind the knight, like d8, stay out of reach.

feedback_by_move.d1d4: Rd4 stops one square short. A rook may capture the first enemy piece on its line, and Rxd5 is legal.
feedback_by_move.d1d8: The rook cannot go through the knight, so d8 cannot be reached.

items.prompt: White to move. Win the queen if there is a way.

claims.statement: The knight on b1 can reach exactly a3, c3 and d2, though a2, b2 and c2 stand next to it.
The queen on d2 is attacked and undefended.
Nxd2 wins the queen.
Nxd2 is the engine's best move.

hints: Count the knight's landing squares, ignoring the pawns beside it.
Does the knight attack the queen's square?
A knight lands on its target no matter what stands between.
items.explain: Pawns on a2, b2 and c2 are next to the knight but do not block it: a knight jumps. It attacks d2, where the queen has no defender, so Nxd2 wins it.

feedback_by_move.a2a3: A pawn move treats the knight as blocked, but the knight can jump to d2. Waiting lets the queen escape or capture.

items.prompt: White to move. The knight is in the corner. Is anything within its reach?

claims.statement: From the corner the knight has just two landing squares, b3 and c2.
Nxc2 wins the queen.
Nb3 is far worse than Nxc2.
Nxc2 is the engine's best move.

hints: Count how many squares the corner knight can reach.
One of them holds a black piece.
Check whether that piece is defended.
items.explain: In the corner the knight has only two landing squares, b3 and c2. One of them holds the undefended queen, so Nxc2 takes it.

feedback_by_move.a1b3: Nb3 is one of the knight's two squares, but it leaves the queen alone, and the engine rates it far below Nxc2.

items.prompt: White to move. Is there a tactic here that wins material, or is this a quiet position?

claims.statement: No line wins more than a pawn for White.
Bxf7+ is far worse than the best move.
Bxf7+ is a legal move.

hints: List the checks and captures White has, then look at the reply to each.
Take the capture on f7 first: who recaptures, and what is left on the board?
If every forcing move loses something, say so.
items.explain: White has a bishop that can take on f7 with check, but the engine rates that capture far below the best moves, and no line wins more than a pawn. Not every position holds a tactic; sometimes the right choice is a plain developing move.

feedback_by_move.c4f7: Bxf7+ looks forcing, but the king takes and White has nothing further: the engine rates it far below a quiet move.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: Each of these moves is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best.
Bxh7+ is much worse than the best move.
Bxh7+ is a legal move.

hints: Before sacrificing, count what each side has near the king.
Which black pieces guard h7 and the squares around the king?
Bxh7+ is legal; ask what happens after the knight takes.
items.explain: The bishop can take on h7 with check, but a knight on f6 takes it back, and the engine rates Bxh7+ much worse than a quiet move. A pattern that works elsewhere has to be checked in this position.

feedback_by_move.d3h7: Bxh7+ does not work here: the knight on f6 can take the bishop, and the engine rates the move much worse than a quiet one.

items.prompt: Black to move. The board is shown from Black's side. Take the bishop standing on c4 with a pawn.

claims.statement: A white bishop stands on c4.
A white pawn stands on f5, not a bishop.
dxc4 is legal and captures the bishop.
exf5 is legal but captures the pawn on f5.
dxc4 wins the bishop for nothing worse than a pawn.

hints: The names stay on their squares even when the board is turned around.
Say the file letter first, then count the rank from White's side.
Black's pawn on d5 is next to the target square.
items.explain: Square names do not change when the board is turned: c4 is file c, rank 4, wherever it appears on the screen. The bishop is on c4, so dxc4 takes it. The pawn capture exf5 takes the pawn on f5 instead.

feedback_by_move.e6f5: exf5 is a legal capture, but it takes the pawn on f5. The bishop is on c4: file c, rank 4.

items.prompt: White to move in a quiet position. Pick a safe move.

claims.statement: Each of these moves is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best.
g4 is far worse than the best move.
g4 is a legal move.

hints: A pawn move cannot be undone. List what it stops guarding.
Which black pieces can use the squares the g-pawn leaves?
The bishop on c8 looks at the kingside once the pawn has left g2.
items.explain: Moving the pawn from g2 to g4 weakens the squares around White's king, and the engine rates it far below several quiet piece or flank moves. A pawn move in front of the king is not safe just because it is a pawn move.

feedback_by_move.g2g4: g4 looks active but leaves the king's pawn cover with holes the black pieces can use; the engine rates it far below a quiet move.

items.prompt: White to move, with about twenty seconds left on the clock. Choose your move.

claims.statement: Qe3 and Kb1 are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best.
Nxe5 is far worse than the best move.
Rxd6 is far worse than the best move.

hints: With little time, name the opponent's reply to each capture before you play it.
Two captures are on the board, both look free. Check what recaptures.
Pick the move that does not give anything away.
items.explain: Two captures look free at a glance, but each loses a piece to a recapture, and the engine rates both far below the quiet moves. Under time pressure the first idea is the one most likely to skip the opponent's reply.

feedback_by_move.f3e5: Nxe5 takes a pawn, but the d6 pawn takes the knight back; the engine rates it far below a quiet move.
feedback_by_move.d1d6: Rxd6 takes a pawn, but it is recaptured; the engine rates it far below a quiet move.

items.prompt: Silent item: no hint is shown until you answer. Write down how sure you are before you move. Black to move: save the half point.

claims.statement: After Kc7 the position is a draw.
After Kd7 Black loses.
After Ke7 Black loses.
After Ke8 Black loses.

hints: Name the square the pawn wants to reach and who guards it.
A king move can stop the pawn only if it is next to the pawn's path.
One move attacks the pawn itself.
items.explain: Kc7 stands next to the pawn and next to its promotion square, so after b8=Q+ the king takes the queen; the tablebase confirms a draw. The other king moves lose. Whether you can do this unprompted shows up in a silent trial like this one, not in a label.

feedback_by_move.d8d7: Kd7 walks toward the pawn but is not next to it or to b8; the tablebase says Black loses.
feedback_by_move.d8e7: Ke7 moves away from the pawn's path; the tablebase says Black loses.
